messages:
incident-bot: INC — High p95 latency and error spike on runtime-continuous-batcher in us-west-2. Error rate 4.2% (CUDA OOM). PagerDuty triggered.

sanjay: getting paged, looking now. seeing batch queue depth spike on batcher-01 -> accumulator growing.

tess: I'm on logs, seeing repeated "cuda: out of memory" from container runtime; node flaps on batcher-pool-3.

ops-bot: autoscaler: spun up 2 replacement nodes due to crashloop; warmup delay ~30s.

sanjay: mitigation plan: set batching.max_batch_tokens=0 on route /generate to disable continuous batching, and drain affected nodes.

lucy: +1, roll command? I can apply a temporary config via runtime-config if you want.

sanjay: doing it now: ```curl -XPOST https://console/api/v1/runtime-config -d '{"route":"/generate","batching":{"max_batch_tokens":0}}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'``` 

deploy-bot: deploy request received, change applied to 3 hosts in us-west-2 in 16s.

tess: latency dropped from 2.1s p95 to 350ms, error rate down to 0.3%. nodes still showing paging pressure; one node in pool in restart-loop.

oncall-ryan: taking over handoff from sanjay, @sanjay please add notes for postmortem and customer impact. I'll coordinate live mitigation.

sanjay: notes: suspected regression in continuous-batcher commit cfa3b9 that changed prefix coalescing; it allowed unlimited accumulator growth on backpressure. Also KV prefetch ramping concurrently.

lucy: copied logs to incidents S3: s3://redwood-incidents/1765234567/batcher-logs.tar.gz

customer-support-bot: customer-impact: ~1200 requests failed between 15:22-15:29 UTC across 8 tenants, top affected customer 'acme-pay' reported increased latency causing checkout timeouts (support ticket #2219).

oncall-ryan: immediate next steps: 1) keep batching disabled, 2) cordon & drain crashloop node, 3) revert cfa3b9 in canary and run integration, 4) run leak reproduction locally with stress harness, 5) prepare customer comms draft.

sanjay: I'm creating a canary with revert now, will attach PR and CI link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/762

tess: monitoring memory, CPU, page-faults. adding alert for batcher.accumulator.size > 50k.

ops-bot: node node-172 terminated due to OOM-Killer, container exited with status 137.

lucy: confirm we should keep Dedicated customers routed to fallback model? suggestion: route heavy customers to lower-throughput variant to reduce queueing.

oncall-ryan: yes route 'premium' to model-small-quantized for now. I'll run routing-change: ```rb router update --route /generate --policy 'if customer==premium then model=model-small-quantized else default'``` 

deploy-bot: routing update applied.

sanjay: started memory profiling dump on batcher-02: ```gcore -o /tmp/core.$(date +%s) $(pidof batcher)``` logs pushed to S3.

tess: we'll capture heap and KV cache stats. preliminary root cause: accumulator didn't respect max_pending_batch_size when under IO pause; leads to unbounded prefetch.

oncall-ryan: customer comms: I'll draft a note tagging support and AMs. @sanjay add impact numbers and timeline. we should schedule a postmortem tomorrow 10:00 PST.

sanjay: added timeline to incident doc: https://wiki.redwood/infrastructure/incidents/1765234567

oncall-ryan: closing loop: keep batching off until root-cause PR merged and validated. assign followups: runtime/bugfix (sanjay), loadtest (lucy), release coord (tess), customer comms (ryan).

tess: adding retrospective ticket and assigning owners. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: incident resolved: traffic normalized at 15:41 UTC, error rate baseline restored. Incident severity downgraded to SEV3.

sanjay: thx all. postmortem will include mitigation playbook and automated kill-switch for continuous-batcher if accumulator > threshold.

oncall-ryan: thanks team, handing back to next oncall @weekend-rotation. please ping if regressions show up.

(reacts: :thumbsup: by lucy, :eyes: by tess)
